title: Chapter 1044
paragraphs: Chapter 1044
Episode 249. The Deployment of the Plutonian (11)
As a precaution, Kaio took care of the three fallen priests. Holding all three with one hand, he resembled a hunter with captured rabbits.
Ban separately took care of the Sun energy, which had transformed into a sphere.
“It better not be nonsense, Sun God religion human.”

“O-of course. I was a... I was a rather zealous believer. That’s why I was able to stay in the first temple, despite not being resurrected through grace. The priestess had granted me quite a lot of authority.”
“Just for being zealous, they gave you that much authority? If that's true, your Sun God religion seems rather lax. You betrayed them quite easily, after all.”
The priest seemed embarrassed and lowered his head.

“Once a non-combat priest like me entered the temple, it was thought that we wouldn’t leave until the Sun God returned… I believed that too. Above all, the priestess emphasized the importance of ordinary believers like me, not just the undead.”
“So, the faith of the living is related to the resurrection of the Sun God.”
“That’s right, Lord Ban. Apart from the first temple, the other temples, especially the third and fourth, have many ordinary believers like me.”
“I’ll offer them the same conditions as you. This priestess Sanna, is she the leader of your sect?”

“No, the Sun God religion doesn’t have a separate leader. We only serve the Sun God. But compared to other religions, it’s fair to say the priestess played the role of a leader. She heard the voice of the Lord and conveyed it to us.”
“What kind of things did she convey?”

“Laws that the believers must follow… or the locations where the physical body of the Sun God is resting. Then, the high priest and combat priests secure them. The sacred body you have now was obtained that way.”
They gathered the flesh of the dead Sun God to resurrect him.
This was the method chosen by the Sun God religion to bring back the Sun God Kinzelo. Hence, the priestess encouraged the various powers to destroy the world in search of the flesh.
“Do you know how many fragments have been secured?”

“I don’t know the exact amount. However, there was a significant recent change within the sect. The priestess and the high priest received some important revelation from the Sun God through a living weapon they secured.”
Ban stopped. The meaning of 'living weapon' was clear.
'Temar’s left arm…?'
During the rescue of Eltiot, Jin had encountered Temar's left arm and the mine 'Temar Bement', created using it, in the underworld.
The Sun God religion currently possessed both the Airen Bement and Temar Bement, and Ban was aware of this.
Friend.
For Ban, Temar was the only friend. Her friend, who died a thousand years ago, was still being used and suffering at the hands of enemies, unable to rest.

'Temar, the Sun God’s will showed great interest in him, especially in relation to his resurrection. Considering Temar’s uniqueness, it’s a plausible story. It was predicted right after Eltiot  was rescued.'
Ban calmed her anger and nodded. The priest, watching her and the Battle Kings brothers’ reactions, guided them towards the second temple.
"Ah, fortunately, it’s not destroyed!"

There was an entrance to the underground in the southeast of the temple. The thick iron door was so dented from the battle that it was unrecognizable, but the transportation device inside was still shining brightly. It was a Sun God religion temple-exclusive transportation device found in the voids.
When the priest lightly tapped the device with a staff, a white dimensional door opened. It was a portal leading to the second temple.
The Plutonian boldly entered the portal. After a flash of light, the group faced the same scene as in the first temple, but the second temple was almost entirely burning.
A battle had already taken place.
The priest looked at the blazing second temple in dismay, while the Plutonian quickly assessed the situation.
Especially Ban, feeling a familiar yet strange energy as soon as she arrived, widened her eyes and screamed.
"Temar!"
The energy felt familiar because it was Temar's power, and strange because it was mixed with the Sun God’s power.
Fusion.
Ban immediately realized that something like this had happened. A bizarre being, a fusion of Temar’s left arm and the Sun energy, was destroying the second temple.
“Ugh…!”
Focusing on that energy, Ban suddenly clutched her radiant heart in agony.
"Battle God brothers!"
"Are you alright?"
The Sun energy, leftover from the battle with Nirgand and Luke, was infiltrating Ban like poison. Ban was aware of it but deemed it not problematic.
But now, the situation had changed.
‘Temar, or rather, the monster using his body, is controlling the Sun energy that infiltrated me.’
Especially the Sun energy recently obtained from Luke was stirring violently. However, Ban couldn’t just discard it. Doing so would immediately threaten the brothers with the Sun energy sphere.
Ban calmly organized her energy and directed her brothers.

"Something's wrong. There's a dangerous entity formed by the fusion of Temar's body and the Sun energy. Brothers, avoid combat with it and secure a dimensional portal to other Sun God religion temples or to the Human world."
"Understood!"
"Lord Ban, I am well-acquainted with the devices of the second temple! The western area seems to be undestroyed, so I'll check the remaining devices there with these men."
Ban immediately sent her brothers and the priest to the western side of the temple. Then she swiftly moved forward, tracking Temar's energy.
Along the way, she stepped over the corpses of the believers. Like those in the first temple who had encountered Ban, they appeared to have been killed without resistance.
As the energy grew closer, the pain in her radiant heart intensified. Soon, Ban saw a mine with golden wings like a veil, Temar Bement, rising in the middle of the temple.
He held a sword identical to Barisada in his right hand and the corpse-like Airen Bement in his left.
Below him, a wounded priestess was screaming.
"Temar Bement, this mine... what are you doing!"
[Accept destruction, priestess. Even if I weren't here, you wouldn't have been able to stop that person today.]
Temar Bement, without even glancing at the priestess, spoke while looking at Ban.
Until recently, the priestess had realized the turmoil in the first temple and was preparing to escape. Then, suddenly, Temar Bement, who was 'blessed' in the basement, began attacking the temple.
It was incomprehensible to the priestess.

She had received a revelation to prepare for the resurrection of the Sun God with Temar Bement at the center, and Temar Bement had not shown any reluctance in receiving the sacred bodies the Sun God religion had gathered.
On the contrary, he seemed quite satisfied, but then suddenly changed.
"Temar Bement! The Sun God blessed you, a mere mine, with revelations. How could you betray that grace... Aaaaack!"
Crack! With a sweep of his hand in the air, the priestess's legs twisted and entwined.
[Blind fool. That’s why you met such a futile end. Even though the being you worshiped is right in front of you, do I still appear to you as a mere useful tool that you were luckily to obtain?]
"How could... If you are the manifestation of the Sun God, the one who spoke to me, why would you do this to me!"
[Priestess, wait for the world’s completion. Everything will flow as it should, and everything will be in its rightful place.]
At these words, the priestess's eyes widened. The eyes filled with doubt, distrust, and anger quickly calmed.
Soon, only faith remained in those dark eyes.
Eventually, the priestess crawled on the floor towards Temar Bement. With a face filled with ecstasy, she prayed, despite the pain of her intertwined legs.
"I offer you everything I have."

The priestess's body, tinged with gold, turned into particles and dispersed. The particles, swirling like dust, were absorbed by Temar Bement. They were the flesh of the Sun God that she had harbored.
Still, Temar Bement's eyes remained fixed on Ban. He had no interest in the priestess who had just sacrificed herself and passed her flesh to him.
Ban organized her radiant heart while trying to understand what and who he was.
Not Temar, but a part of Sun God Kinzelo, manifested using his body.
In a sense, one aspect of the original creator god.
[I see you're displeased that I'm using the name Temar, Ban.]
He instantly read Ban’s emotions.
"The body you've manifested in should have rested long ago. It belonged to my friend. You've only borrowed Temar’s body; you're not him."
[To you, it was a long time ago, but to me, it was just a moment. Call me Bligiet. I, too, do not wish to use the name of a mortal.]
Bligiet, one of the many names once used to denote the Sun God.
"A considerate god indeed. Did you avoid Kinzelo because it's practically synonymous with a failed collective?"
[It's my failed creation; the ugliest name of all. Sadly, the mortals who claim to serve me use it.]
Ban paid attention to Airen, held in Bligiet’s hand.
"You claim to be the mightiest god, the only god, yet you still need that body and the corpse of the Airen Bement."
[Embarrassing, but unavoidable.]
With each word Bligiet spoke, pain spread through Ban's radiant heart, threatening to shatter it apart from the pain, Ban also sensed a kind of nobility in Bligiet, similar to that of a witch.
[You may not realize it, but you attracted my attention more than Temar, the owner of this body, ever did. Had it not been for Soldelet, I would have appeared in this world through you.]
Sigmund emerged from its sheath. However, Bligiet had no intention of fighting her.

[Do you think you can cut me with that sword? You know best that it's impossible. I am about to go and release the constraints that Airen Bement left on this body. It's ironic that this insect held everything of mine...]
Upon hearing this, Ban instinctively thought of a particular group. Ziffle, it seemed likely that Bligiet would seek them out.
"Is that so? Thanks for letting me know."
Sssht-! A streak of blue sword energy flew towards Bligiet. It didn't reach him, but it cut off Airen, who was attached to his hand like a fruit.
The lower half of Iren, cut by the sword energy, fell to the ground.
[...Strange, you shouldn't be able to attack me.]
Bligiet shook his head as if in shock, and Ban once again wrapped her sword with sword energy.
